theme: Graphite GPU, Nano Server fonts, perf
highlights_headline: Adds the Graphite GPU backend, Nano Server FreeType fonts, and multiple allocation-free performance improvements.
highlights_body: ramezgerges contributes Graphite backend bindings spanning Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn. jeffska adds FreeType-backed font support for Nano Server containers, closing a long-standing gap. A new Vulkan Silk.NET package, async pixel reads, and several managed-layer perf wins complete the release.

bullets.detail: Three rounds of upstream chrome/m151 bug-fix merges keep the bundled engine in sync with Skia's stable branch.

bullets.lead: Graphite GPU backend for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn
bullets.detail: New bindings expose the Graphite rendering backend across all three GPU APIs, giving consumers access to SkiaSharp's next-generation GPU path alongside the existing Ganesh backend.

bullets.lead: Async RequestReadPixels on SKImage and SKSurface
bullets.detail: A backend-neutral async pixel-read API lets GPU-resident images and surfaces deliver pixel data without blocking the render thread.
A dedicated package wires SkiaSharp's Vulkan backend to the Silk.NET Vulkan bindings, simplifying setup for consumers already using Silk.NET.
Binding generation now produces identical output regardless of the host platform, making reproduced builds byte-for-byte consistent across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

bullets.lead: CoTaskMem pixel-buffer leak in SKImage.Create raster failure path
bullets.detail: When the native raster image creation failed after allocating the pixel buffer, the unmanaged memory was not freed. The leak is now plugged.

bullets.lead: Windows native build MSVC environment initialized once
bullets.detail: The MSVC toolchain environment is now set up once per native build session instead of once per target, avoiding redundant shell overhead on Windows CI.

bullets.lead: FreeType font support for Windows Nano Server
bullets.detail: Nano Server containers can now render text using a bundled FreeType font engine, closing a long-standing gap (issue #1105) for server-side headless rendering.

bullets.lead: Containerized test coverage: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, Nano Server
bullets.detail: New CI legs run the SkiaSharp test suite inside Docker containers targeting Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Windows Nano Server, verifying the native assets on these platforms.
All SkiaSharp solution files are converted to the new XML-based .slnx format, reducing merge conflicts and improving IDE load times.

bullets.lead: SKData.SaveTo no longer copies through a double buffer
bullets.detail: The previous implementation copied the data into an intermediate byte[] before writing; it now writes directly from the native buffer, halving memory traffic for large saves.
The uniform lookup map is pre-sized to the known count, and the null-terminated GetEncodedText path avoids an intermediate string allocation, reducing per-call heap pressure.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: FreeType-backed font support for Nano Server containers, closing a multi-year rendering gap for Windows headless environments.
contributor_summaries.mmitche: Windows native build robustness: MSVC environment initialized once per build session instead of redundantly per target.
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn — bringing SkiaSharp's next-generation rendering path into managed code.
